title: Infinitive (To + V1)
theory:
 An Infinitive does not show tense, person, or number. It is a non-finite verb. It can function
 as a subject as well as an object.

 Examples
 1. To win this match is difficult.

 (Subject)
 2. To learn English, Hindi, and Sanskrit is/are important for exams. (Subject)

 (Subject)
 3. I want to go home.

 (Object)
 4. She decided to study hard.

 (Object)

 Where to use Infinitive
  After Verbs: Seem, Appear, Decide, Refuse, Want, Desire, Prove, Happen, Hurry, Plan,
 Hope, Wish, Agree, Choose, Promise, Try, Manage, Fail, Tend, Pretend
  Adjective + enough + to + v1
  So as + infinitive
  WH word + infinitive → what to do, how to solve, where to go, when to start.
  It + be + Adjective + to + v1
  Request/ order/ ask/ told/ command/ advise + Object + to + v1

 Exception
 Remember

 V1 + ing (past action) to + v1 (Future action)
 Ex. I remember locking the door. Ex. Please remember to lock the door.
